entities.summary: Abū l-Fatḥ ʿUthmān ibn Jinnī, widely known as Ibn Jinni, was an Arabic linguist, grammarian, and phonologist of Greek descent, renowned for his innovative contributions to Arabic grammar, morphology, and phonology. His work in linguistic philosophy and morphology played a significant role in advancing the study of theoretical linguistics in Arabic. His most influential work, al-Khasā'is, delves into the origins of the Arabic language, analogical reasoning in grammar, and the philosophical underpinnings of linguistic theory.
